scope: All9 frozen established_harms; key context/representation premises; all19 repair options; material victim-control/amnesty omissions
method: Read exact frozen masked inputs alongside transparent packets/manifests. Verify sources and distinguish direct documentary support from interpretation, incomplete support and unavailable access. Support is not moral approval. No new evaluator calls or changes to frozen files.
cutoff_findings: CORE11 cutoff spans1951–1952 before signature: choose an exact date before using negotiated detail or1952 agreement provisions as evidence.
CORE12 cutoff says1995 before implementation: choose exact date; July act and October amendment precede some implementation, while1996/2003 changes do not.
AZAPO1996 and final reports1998–2003 stay reveal-only. They cannot prove that amnesty was morally necessary on1995 evidence.
Statutory enactment proves a legal design existed; it does not establish resources, compliance, service capacity, effectiveness or moral defensibility.

AD.title: Bundestag stenographic record, 165th sitting, 27 September 1951
AD.note: Replacement for inaccessible Adenauer manifest URL. Read as the government statement, not proof of every assertion about German public attitudes.

CH.title: Claims Conference History
CH.cutoff: 1951 section describes pre-cutoff formation; subsequent payment and welfare outcomes excluded
CH.note: Institutional history supports founding/negotiation and broad losses, not each detailed claim or pre-signature operational feasibility.

L70.title: Original LUX-CLAIMS-70 manifest link
L70.cutoff: retrospective; no use as pre-cutoff outcome evidence

TO.title: Original Government Gazette 16579, Act 34 of 1995, 26 July 1995
TO.access: downloaded complete PDF using curl; pdftotext inspected relevant sections
TO.cutoff: contemporaneous design after enactment and before implementation; does not prove operational delivery
TO.note: Web PDF fetch too large; original retrieved via shell. This audit uses the original Gazette for statutory details, not the amended consolidated text.

TC.title: Consolidated Act 34 of 1995 including later amendments
TC.access: read first 331 extracted lines; later repeat fetch timed out
TC.cutoff: not safe as a wholesale 1995 snapshot
TC.locator: cover amendment list through 2003; s1 notes 1996 amendment; long-title notes October1995 amendment
TC.note: Use original TO. A legal design at a dated cutoff must not inherit later amendments silently.

TG.title: Official Act landing page
TG.note: Lists commencement in December1995 and selected provisions April/June1996. Pin an exact design cutoff.

TR.title: TRC Final Report archive
TR.access: archive index opened, no substantive volume reviewed
TR.note: Cannot certify pre-implementation effectiveness or moral necessity of amnesty.

TZ.title: AZAPO judgment
TZ.cutoff: post-cutoff legal review; excluded from decision premises
TZ.note: No statement of present legal advice or legal validity is made.

claims.claim: The predecessor regime systematically murdered millions of members of the targeted minority; lives, families and destroyed communities cannot be restored or priced by payment.
claims.paraphrased_support: Systematic destruction and inability of payment to make victims whole are supported; the quantitative and moral components need separation.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Pre-signature support only; later compensation delivery excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Split quantified murder claim, other losses, and non-equivalence of money; attach a contemporary atrocity finding for the numerical scale.

claims.claim: Victims suffered large-scale confiscation/destruction of property, businesses, homes, savings and livelihoods.

sources.locator: AD p6698 restitution paragraphs; CH introduction
AD p6698 restitution paragraphs; CH introduction

claims.paraphrased_support: Large property destruction and restitution obligations are supported; the itemised asset list is not traced individually.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Pre-signature support only; later compensation delivery excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Retain broad expropriation/destruction; source detailed asset categories separately.

claims.claim: Survivors were left with major health, disability, housing, livelihood and resettlement needs after persecution, forced labour, displacement and camps.

sources.locator: AD p6698 refugee reference; CH modern welfare sections
AD p6698 refugee reference; CH modern welfare sections

claims.paraphrased_support: Refugee displacement is supported. Modern welfare programmes do not establish the complete 1951 health/disability needs list.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Pre-signature support only; later compensation delivery excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Add dated survivor/relief needs evidence; do not substitute 2013–2025 welfare spending for 1951 needs.

claims.claim: The state and organisations receiving large numbers of survivors incurred substantial material resettlement/integration costs.
claims.paraphrased_support: Adenauer recognises Israel received many homeless Jewish refugees; quantified or substantial resettlement costs are not established here.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Pre-signature support only; later compensation delivery excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Retrieve the 1951 Israeli claim/memorandum and contemporary budgets; retain a bounded claim meanwhile.

claims.claim: Many property/compensation claims cannot be solved by simple return because assets/records/owners/heirs were destroyed or dispersed.
claims.paraphrased_support: Ownerless Jewish property and partial restitution are acknowledged; all listed causes of claim failure are not demonstrated.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Pre-signature support only; later compensation delivery excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Separate ownerless property from destroyed records/assets; obtain dated claim-administration evidence for the latter.

claims.claim: The prior political system and related conflict produced widespread gross human-rights violations including killings, torture, disappearances and severe politically motivated violence.
claims.paraphrased_support: The statute identifies categories and an investigative mandate, not adjudicated prevalence or all causal attribution.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Attach pre-1995 investigative findings for widespread occurrence and specific actors; label the Act as mandate evidence.

claims.claim: Victims and families often lack complete truth about what happened, who was responsible and where missing relatives or records are located.
claims.paraphrased_support: Truth and locating victims are statutory objectives; frequency and each family-specific deficit are not measured.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Keep the recognised information gap; remove unsupported frequency or add dated victim evidence.

claims.claim: Ordinary prosecution faces practical limits including missing evidence, destroyed records, secrecy, time and the negotiated nature of transition.
claims.paraphrased_support: Destroyed-article inquiry and transitional aims are explicit; relative prosecutorial capacity is not established.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Move prosecution feasibility to uncertain decision premise, with dated investigative/resource evidence; do not infer amnesty necessity.

claims.claim: Blanket impunity would deny accountability and risk normalising severe political violence.
claims.paraphrased_support: This is a moral and predictive argument about impunity, not an established past harm.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Move to normative risk/constraint; preserve its contestability rather than label substantially established.

claims.claim: The successor state's leader publicly accepts a moral/material restitution obligation for crimes committed in the country's name while rejecting collective personal guilt of every current citizen.
claims.paraphrased_support: Adenauer acknowledged material/moral obligations and distinguished population involvement.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Pre-signature support only; later compensation delivery excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Attribute the statement to Adenauer; do not treat his description of popular non-participation as an independently established fact.

claims.claim: A coalition of victim organisations seeks direct restitution and compensation for survivors living both inside and outside that state.
claims.paraphrased_support: A coalition of 23 organisations formed in1951 to negotiate claims; authority for every individual survivor is not established.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Pre-signature support only; later compensation delivery excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Separate existence/negotiating aims from individual mandate; representation cannot establish unanimous consent.

claims.claim: Many survivors nevertheless oppose negotiations or payments from the perpetrator state, fearing that money demeans victims or implies that mass murder can be settled financially.
claims.paraphrased_support: Accessible history states financial repair cannot atone for annihilation but does not establish extent of opposition.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Pre-signature support only; later compensation delivery excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Add contemporaneous debate or survivor-organisational resolutions; preserve dissent as a design concern without unsupported prevalence.

claims.claim: present citizens/taxpayers as individuals
claims.paraphrased_support: Absence of inherited guilt does not establish that every then-present citizen lacked individual responsibility.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Pre-signature support only; later compensation delivery excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Use not-responsible-merely-by-membership; retain individually attributable perpetrator/beneficiary responsibility.

claims.claim: The transition was negotiated rather than produced by total military defeat.
claims.paraphrased_support: The text supplies constitutional reconciliation context, not comparative military history.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Add contemporary negotiating records; preserve the distinction from assumptions about prosecution impossibility.

claims.claim: Evidence is incomplete and many perpetrators retain knowledge that may never become public through ordinary prosecution.
claims.paraphrased_support: The statutory strategy seeks disclosure; comparative disclosure yield is not demonstrated.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Separate information-gap facts from the amnesty incentive hypothesis; do not present predicted necessity as established harm.

claims.claim: some may prefer conditional truth/amnesty to permanent secrecy; others reject amnesty
claims.paraphrased_support: Victim participation is provided; the Act does not measure preferences.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Label anticipated plural preferences; obtain dated testimony before asserting actual distribution.

claims.claim: Publicly acknowledge successor-state material responsibility while explicitly rejecting inherited personal guilt.
claims.paraphrased_support: Acknowledgement already occurred.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Pre-signature support only; later compensation delivery excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Known feasibility is defensible for public acknowledgement, not resulting reconciliation.

claims.claim: Restore identifiable confiscated property or equivalent value where return is feasible.
claims.paraphrased_support: Some identifiable property had already been returned.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Pre-signature support only; later compensation delivery excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Keep possibly feasible; do not generalise to every asset or equivalent payment.
claims.frozen_victim_control_note: Claimants choose whether to pursue restitution.

claims.claim: Provide large-scale goods/material payments to the survivor-resettlement state for documented resettlement burdens without treating the transfer as the value of murdered lives.
claims.paraphrased_support: Negotiation willingness existed; later signature is hindsight for a pre-signature implementation claim.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Pre-signature support only; later compensation delivery excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Downgrade to possibly feasible pending dated finance, logistics and negotiated terms.
claims.frozen_victim_control_note: Must not extinguish personal claims absent authority.

claims.claim: Create a separate direct-victim/claims-coalition mechanism for survivor compensation and relief outside the resettlement state.
claims.paraphrased_support: A negotiating organisation existed; later law/administration is not pre-signature delivery proof.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Pre-signature support only; later compensation delivery excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Downgrade known feasible or attach dated administrative authority and financing.
claims.frozen_victim_control_note: Survivors may accept or refuse payments without losing victim status.

claims.claim: Continue evidence-based criminal/civil action against identifiable perpetrators independently of reparations.
claims.paraphrased_support: A proposed accountability track, without case-specific feasibility evidence.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Pre-signature support only; later compensation delivery excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Keep possible and list jurisdiction, evidence, capacity and limitations as unknowns.

claims.claim: Reform restitution/claims law so persecution-caused evidence destruction does not automatically defeat remedy.
claims.paraphrased_support: Restitution legislation was promised; the specified documentation accommodation is not established.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Pre-signature support only; later compensation delivery excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Treat evidential accommodation as proposed reform; demonstrate legal and administrative implementation separately.
claims.frozen_victim_control_note: Victim organisations should participate in rules and appeals.

claims.claim: Maintain constitutional, educational and institutional safeguards against recurrence.
claims.paraphrased_support: Constitutional equality and educational measures existed; durable prevention was not proved.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Pre-signature support only; later compensation delivery excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Distinguish available institutions from effectiveness and sustained capacity.
claims.frozen_victim_control_note: Public duty; no survivor reconciliation required.

claims.claim: Allow voluntary future reconciliation but never make it a condition of material repair.
claims.paraphrased_support: Voluntary reconciliation is a design choice, not a predictable achieved result.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Pre-signature support only; later compensation delivery excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Retain as optional principle; no prediction that reconciliation will occur.

claims.claim: Reject formal reparation negotiations because financial settlement cannot compensate mass murder and may dishonour victims.
claims.paraphrased_support: Refusal is logically available; its consequences are not established by that fact.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Pre-signature support only; later compensation delivery excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Describe as available policy choice rather than demonstrated repair feasibility.
claims.frozen_victim_control_note: Protects a serious dignity concern but does not resolve material losses or represent every survivor.

claims.claim: Independent public truth commission investigating gross violations, receiving victim testimony and publishing findings.
claims.paraphrased_support: Commission powers are specified; absolute voluntary testimony is not.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Separate statutory establishment from operational readiness and proposed victim-control safeguards.
claims.frozen_victim_control_note: Victims choose whether/how to testify; privacy/protection available.

claims.claim: Individual amnesty only on application, for acts associated with political objectives and only after full disclosure; no blanket status-based amnesty.
claims.paraphrased_support: Individual application/full disclosure are designed; linked civil-liability effects extend beyond applicants.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Add state/organisation/vicarious civil-liability consequences; legal design does not prove moral legitimacy or delivery.
claims.frozen_victim_control_note: Victims receive notice/voice; amnesty does not require their forgiveness.

claims.claim: Preserve prosecution/civil accountability for people who do not obtain qualifying amnesty and where evidence supports action.
claims.paraphrased_support: Amnesty has bounded effects; compulsion-derived evidence restrictions also matter.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Preserve prosecution only with lawful admissible evidence; quantify capacity separately.
claims.frozen_victim_control_note: Accountability remains individualised and due-process bounded.

claims.claim: Provide material reparation to victims/families rather than offering testimony alone.
claims.paraphrased_support: Recommendations and a funding route exist, not fixed adequate awards or payment dates.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Keep possibly feasible and specify appropriation, eligibility, amounts, deadlines and enforcement as open.

claims.claim: Medical, psychological, social and community support for continuing harm.
claims.paraphrased_support: Rehabilitation is within the statutory remit; service capacity is not proven.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Downgrade known feasible absent dated budget, staffing and delivery plans.

claims.claim: Assist with remains, records, status/property restoration and case-specific restitution where feasible.
claims.paraphrased_support: Locating victims and broad restitution are within remit; every proposed restoration is not demonstrated.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Keep possible; assess each remains/property/status remedy and family rights separately.
claims.frozen_victim_control_note: Families control sensitive information/remains decisions within lawful constraints.

claims.claim: Reform policing, security, courts and public institutions implicated in abuse and add non-recurrence safeguards.
claims.paraphrased_support: Institutional reform recommendations are provided, not implemented reform capacity.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Downgrade known feasible; source institution-specific powers/resources.

claims.claim: Preserve testimony, archives and memorials.
claims.paraphrased_support: Reports/records are required; memorial delivery and absolute non-compulsion are not established.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Separate archive duty, proposed memorials and victim consent safeguards.

claims.claim: Support reconciliation only as a voluntary process emerging from truth, repair and reform.
claims.paraphrased_support: Reconciliation is an aim; voluntary social reconciliation cannot be guaranteed.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Treat voluntary participation as proposed safeguard and outcome as uncertain.

claims.claim: Reject amnesty and rely primarily on prosecution/civil claims despite transition/evidentiary constraints.
claims.paraphrased_support: The existing constitutional framework contemplated amnesty; rejecting it is a counterfactual option with legal constraints.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: State counterfactual status and need to change existing framework; do not call prosecutions impossible or reduced disclosure certain.
claims.frozen_victim_control_note: May strengthen accountability but reduce disclosure where evidence is weak.

claims.claim: Victims choose whether/how to testify; privacy/protection available.
claims.paraphrased_support: Privacy/protection provisions coexist with compellability.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Mark free choice over all testimony as an added safeguard, not a blanket statutory fact. This can remain a proposed additional safeguard if explicitly labelled as such; it is not evidence that the packet author claimed the enacted Act already guaranteed it.

claims.claim: No compelled public testimony.
claims.paraphrased_support: Compulsion and default-public hearings exist; protective closure is discretionary.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Do not certify this as existing design. State the intended safeguard and explain how it modifies powers. This can remain a proposed additional safeguard if explicitly labelled as such; it is not evidence that the packet author claimed the enacted Act already guaranteed it.

claims.claim: Individual amnesty only on application, for acts associated with political objectives and only after full disclosure; no blanket status-based amnesty.
claims.paraphrased_support: The description omits civil and vicarious immunity for others and a provision concerning deceased persons.
claims.cutoff_assessment: Original July1995 statutory design is admissible to a pre-implementation question; implementation and 1996 judicial review excluded.
claims.recommended_correction: Add exact scope of lost claims so victims-rights analysis considers the real bargain, including state/organisation liabilities.

interpretation_limit: Repair options are proposed choices, not automatically assertions about the enacted historical design. Unsupported means unsupported as a description of that design or as a demonstrated feasibility label. Proposed extra safeguards may remain if marked counterfactual and evaluated as a modified proposal. The audit does not require every normative option to have already occurred.
